title: audit the France state-resolution contradiction: 71.10% vs 97.44%
headline: NOT A CONTRADICTION - the two figures are not the same quantity. D073 measured a dictionary bound (union bound over the 14 FR_REGIONS keys); D077 measured an address-parseability ceiling (empty-address rate) and never consulted FR_REGIONS. They are nested lower bounds on the same unknown and D073's is the tighter. Under one criterion: at most 1,213,296 of 1,694,445 France test rows (71.60%) can resolve a state; at least 481,149 (28.40%) provably cannot. D077's 2.5620% should be retired, not averaged. VERDICT: do not extend FR_REGIONS.
most_important_number_meaning: France test rows that PROVABLY carry no FR_REGIONS-resolvable state = 28.40% of 1,694,445. This is a lower bound (sound direction), reproduced exactly from D073's corrected .md.

criterion.one_sentence: A France test row counts as state-resolved if and only if at least one comma-delimited component of business_address, after translit_text + strip_accents + lowercasing + punctuation-to-space folding, is exactly equal to one of the 14 FR_REGIONS keys.
decisive_properties: line 333 is a WHOLE-COMPONENT exact match; '12 rue de lorraine' != key 'lorraine'
line 335 `continue` means a matching component contributes no tokens
line 317 strips accents BEFORE matching, but build_profile.py does NOT - so the profile UNDERCOUNTS accented keys
criterion_does_NOT_contain: any use of by_country.has_comma (D077 imported this; it is not in the code)

france_rows.scope: France is test-only; country_rows in train_s1..s3 contains only US and India

the_contradiction_resolved.verdict: NOT a contradiction - criterion mismatch, different quantities

d073.question: How many rows can contain a FR_REGIONS key?
d073.test: union bound: per-key min of constituent token counts, summed over 14 keys, clamped per file to min(UB, rows)
d073.direction_of_error: conservative - overlap inflates the union bound
d073.artefact_inconsistency_found: D073's JSON sidecar carries the PRE-fix numbers (1,204,739/71.10%/28.90%); its .md carries the CORRECTED 1,213,296/71.60%/28.40%. The task brief quotes the stale JSON figure. Cite the .md.

d077.question: How many rows are not structurally dead?
d077.produces: ceiling on anything state-like, NOT a resolvability rate
d077.direction_of_error: ANTI-conservative - assumes every non-empty comma-bearing row resolves
d077.self_falsifying_control: D077's own invariant is near country-invariant: US test_s2 97.0552%, US test_s3 97.1570%, India 97.5368%, France 97.4380%. A coverage figure near-identical across disjoint state tables measures ADDRESS FORMAT, not coverage.
d077.recommendation: RETIRE the 2.5620% figure - do not average it with D073's

the_contradiction_resolved.why_both_can_be_true: D077 says >=97.44% of rows are NOT RULED OUT. D073 says <=71.60% of rows are CAPABLE. These are nested lower bounds on the unknown unresolvable fraction and are simultaneously satisfiable.

interval_i_can_defend.reason: profile discards component identity, so token counts cannot be converted to resolved-row counts in either direction

per_key_minima.note: union-bound ingredient; absent tokens substituted with the rank-4000 cutoff (23/58/60); `ile` substituted with max(count(ile), count(le)) to absorb profile accent loss
per_key_minima.clamp_note: s1 UB 263440 > rows 259452, so s1's bound is VACUOUS - it cannot detect anything. This is exactly why the inherited s1-only 100% figure looked fine.

per_source_admin_level.definition: density = token occurrences / France rows. EXCEEDS 100% for s1 because a region name contributes 2-3 tokens per row. Density is a concentration indicator, NOT a row count and NOT coverage.
per_source_admin_level.absence_caveat: not in the top 4000 means count <= 23/58/60, NOT proven absent
per_source_admin_level.interpretation: s1 encodes REGIONS (hence vacuous bound and the inherited s1-only 100% figure); s2/s3 encode DEPARTMENTS whose names (gironde, nord, calais, loire atlantique) are ALREADY keys in FR_REGIONS; the residual is CITY-ONLY addresses carrying no administrative token at all, which no gazetteer can reach.

gazetteer_test.method: identical per-key-minimum union bound, clamped per file to min(UB, rows); token-disjoint subset excludes any key sharing a token with the 20 tokens FR_REGIONS already uses
gazetteer_test.precision_risk: lorraine/alsace are common French street names, grand est/centre/gard are ordinary nouns. Whole-component matching (line 333) limits but does not eliminate this. Precision is UNMEASURABLE from the profile - gap.

gaps: NO COMPONENT STRUCTURE: build_profile.py:126-127 splits on [,;] then updates a FLATTENED counter. Component identity and order are destroyed. Token counts cannot be converted to resolved-row counts in either direction. THIS is why a bound is the correct output, not a failure.

NO ACCENT STRIPPING in profile: TOKEN_RE = [a-z0-9]+ (build_profile.py:28) on the lowercased address, no strip_accents. ile 303/817/794 vs le 1992/4882/5050. Corrected only for `ile`; vendee->vend (53/80/97), cote d or, rhone alpes remain undercounted, so the true UB may be slightly HIGHER than 1,213,296. Direction: 71.60% is conservative.
SEMICOLON MISMATCH: profile splits on [,;], normalize_address splits on ',' only (line 322). Direction of error not cleanly determined.
NO PER-ROW DATA: every figure is a token-occurrence sum. Raw TSVs prohibited on this box.
PRECISION of any candidate key is unmeasurable - can bound rows that COULD resolve, never rows that would FALSELY resolve.

CITY->REGION MAPPING NOT DERIVABLE: addr_tokens holds marginal counts, not co-occurrence. Not estimated. This is the correct next scraping job: re-scan France with component identity preserved, keyed on city.

structural_context.note: D077's 2.5620% is derived from addr_empty + nonempty_comma_free = 43,411. It is a DATA property, not a dictionary property.

inherited_claim_reassessment.claim: state resolves for 100.00% of France rows (259,452 / 259,452)
inherited_claim_reassessment.verdict: REFUTED - true for test_s1 only, which is 15.31% of French rows
inherited_claim_reassessment.note: Close to the prior agent's triple but NOT reproducible from the profile. Conclusion survives regardless: s1 is 15.31% of French rows and the untouched 84.69% drives the whole disagreement.

engineering_verdict.confirms: the fleet brief's existing settled entry - FR_REGIONS needs no dictionary expansion - now with the MECHANISM explained rather than merely asserted
engineering_verdict.reasoning_criterion: whole-comma-component exact match against the 14 FR_REGIONS keys after translit + strip_accents + lowercase + punctuation fold
reasons: the 3 region tokens carrying 89.7% of region mass (hauts/nouvelle/pays) are ALREADY mapped
the 4 department tokens carrying 98.9% of dept mass (nord/gironde/calais/atlantique), which dominate s2/s3, are ALSO already mapped - s2/s3 DO resolve, via the department half of the table

the >=25.76% residual is address-shaped 'number + street + city' with no administrative component, unreachable by any gazetteer; a maximal 49-key gazetteer buys <=2.64 pp on paper and 0.80 pp provably-incremental
engineering_verdict.real_fix: a city->region table (bordeaux/nantes/lille alone are ~43.7% of every French test file) - but NOT derivable from this profile. Gap, not a number.
engineering_verdict.process_recommendation: Any future 'state resolves for X% of rows' claim must state (a) the component-match criterion and (b) the denominator file.
